summary: --docker alone uses the default container, which is recommended for sanity and unit tests. You can name another container right after --docker, or a custom one with --python to state its Python version.
questions: Which container image should I use for ansible-test sanity tests?
How do I list the containers ansible-test supports?
How do I run ansible-test in my own container image?
Why do I need --python with a custom container?

answer_card.title: Choose an ansible-test container
answer_card.answer_md:
- `--docker` alone uses the `default` container, recommended for sanity and unit tests.
- `--docker <name>` picks another supported container. See the list with `ansible-test <command> --help` (it differs per command).
- For your own image, pass it after `--docker` and also give `--python <version>` so ansible-test knows which Python is inside.
